comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose accounting mechanics where the recognition of fair value changes creates timing or presentation mismatches relative to related expense categories. MS specifically discusses a 'timing difference' between the immediate recognition of investment fair value gains/losses in Wealth Management revenues and the deferred recognition of compensation expense for DCP awards. Similarly, C discloses that for certain hybrid financial instruments, the interest expense is reported together with fair value changes in 'Principal transactions' rather than in the standard 'Interest expense' line item. While MS focuses on the impact of timing differences on revenue/expense matching in a specific segment (Wealth Management), C focuses on the presentation classification of expense components for hybrid instruments in Principal transactions. Both disclosures highlight how fair value accounting for specific instruments affects the standard line-item reporting of revenues or expenses.

sentences.text: Although changes in compensation expense resulting from changes in the fair value of the referenced investments will generally be offset by changes in the fair value of investments recognized in net revenues, there is typically a timing difference between the immediate recognition of gains and losses on our investments and the deferred recognition of the related compensation expense over the vesting period.

(2)Interest expense associated with certain hybrid financial instruments, which are classified as Long-term debt and accounted for at fair value, is reported together with any changes in fair value as part of Principal transactions in the Consolidated Statement of Income and is therefore not reflected in Interest expense in the table above.
